sentences.text: A common award was passed by the Tribunal in MVC Nos.982 and 983/2018 dated 09.09.2022.

This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award dated 09.09.2022 passed in MVC No.982/2018 on the file of the XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, MACT, Bengaluru City, for enhancing the compensation.

entities.text: XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, MACT, Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.1.
The ranks of the parties are retained as per tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. The injured claimant met with an accident on 02.02.2018 and filed claim petition claiming compensation NC: 2026:KHC:13838 HC-KAR of Rs.18,00,000.
But the Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted Rs.6,20,747/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

4. Aggrieved by the said order, the claimant preferred an appeal and mainly contended that the Tribunal granted meager amount under the other heads and PW2/doctor assessed the disability as 45% to the right lower limb and 15% to the whole body.
But the Tribunal has erred in taking the disability as 10% instead of 15%.
Also interest is to be granted at the rate of 9%.
Thus, he has requested for enhancement of the compensation.

5. Learned counsel for respondent stated that the injured is an employee in Bata Company and the fractures are united and it was observed by the Tribunal that the disability will not have much impact on the work of petitioner and accordingly the Tribunal rightly considered 10% disability.
So also it is stated that he himself NC: 2026:KHC:13838 HC-KAR admitted that he was earning Rs.12,000/-.
But the Tribunal has taken Rs.12,500/- based on the chart.
Learned counsel for respondent further argued that Tribunal granted excessive amount under pain and suffering, loss of amenities and other heads and it is to be reduced.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the petitioner has not filed any proof of income.
As he met with an accident in the year 2018, his notional income is to be taken as Rs.12,500/- per month.
But he himself admitted that he was getting Rs.12,000/- per month.
But in all cases where there is no proof of income, this Court is relying upon the chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Therefore,
even in this case, as there is no proof of income, this Court finds it reasonable to take his notional income as Rs. 12,500/- as it is a beneficial legislation and whichever is favourable to the litigant is to be considered.
He was aged 19 years and the multiplier to be taken as '18' and as per the evidence of orthopedic surgeon PW2 he NC: 2026:KHC:13838 HC-KAR sustained fracture of shaft femur and he underwent surgery.
Accordingly, assessed the disability of the limb as 45% and whole body as 15%.
Injuries are permanent in nature and he has difficulty in doing daily routine activities.
The doctor further stated that he requires another surgery for removal of the implants and estimated the cost of the surgery as Rs. 30,000/-.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to take 1/3rd of 45% as 15% instead of 10%.

Hence, loss of future income is calculated as Rs.12,500 x 12 x 18 x 15% =
Rs.4,05,000/-.
Further, the injured incurred Rs.1,85,787/- towards medical bills as per Ex.P7 and it is confirmed.
He was admitted in the hospital for a period of 6 days.
The amount granted by the tribunal under the other heads are just and reasonable and it needs no interference.

7. Thus in all, components awarded by this court are as below, NC: 2026:KHC:13838 HC-KAR Particulars Amount Sl.Nos.
in Rs.
1
Loss of future income 4,05,000 2 Pain and suffering 70,000 3 Loss of income during the laid 24,960 up period and attendant charge 4
Conveyance charges 10,000
5 Food nourishment, 40,000 attendant charges and loss of amenities 6
Towards future medical 20,000 expenses 7
Medical bills 1,85,787

Hence, the compensation granted by tribunal is enhanced from Rs.6,20,747/- to Rs.7,55,747/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
8.

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER i.
Appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2026:KHC:13838 HC-KAR ii.
The judgment and award dated 09.09.2022 passed in MVC No.982/2018 on the file of the XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, MACT, Bengaluru City, is modified.

entities.text: XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, MACT, Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: iii. The claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.7,55,747/- along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization, instead of Rs.6,20,747/- granted by the tribunal.
iv. Respondent/Insurance Company has already deposited the awarded amount before the tribunal.
Therefore, respondent/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,35,000/- along with the interest at the rate of 6% within one month from the date of this order.
